desc:
A binary tree was serialized in preorder: the value of every real node is written when the node is visited, followed by the serialization of its left subtree and then of its right subtree, and a missing child is written as -1. Missing children are written for every node that lacks them, so the array describes the tree completely.

Given such an array data, rebuild the tree and return it in the standard level-order encoding.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed (or returned) as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree below: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For data = [1, 2, -1, 4, -1, -1, 3, -1, -1] the answer is [1, 2, 3, -1, 4]. For data = [-1] (the empty tree) the answer is [], and for data = [5, -1, 6, -1, -1] it is [5, -1, 6].
constraints: 1 ≤ data.length ≤ 3,001 (a tree with at most 1,500 nodes has 2n + 1 entries)
Every real value is between 0 and 10,000; missing children are -1
data is a valid serialization: it contains exactly one more -1 than it contains real values, and it ends exactly when the tree is complete
hints: The first entry is the root (or -1 for the empty tree). What must come right after it?
After the root comes the complete serialization of its left subtree, and when that is finished, the complete serialization of its right subtree. A subtree is finished when a missing marker closes it.

Keep a stack of nodes whose children are not yet complete. Each next entry becomes the next free child of the node on top of the stack: first the left slot, then the right slot (after which the parent leaves the stack). A real value is also pushed as a new open node.
editorial: Read the array from left to right and think of every entry as the next child slot to fill. The recursive formulation is: read() takes the next entry; if it is -1 return empty, otherwise create a node whose left child is read() and whose right child is read(). Because the format is self-delimiting, no extra information is needed to find where a subtree ends.

The same thing without recursion keeps a stack of open nodes together with a flag saying whether the left child has been filled. Every entry goes into the left slot, or the right slot of the node on top of the stack, and a node is popped as soon as its right slot is filled; a real value is pushed as a new open node. Each entry is processed once, so the time is linear. Finally the tree is written out level by level as in the other problems.
